newsitem.title: FINLAND: INTERVIEW - FINNISH NOVO SEEKS TO GROW ABOVE MARKET.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - FINNISH NOVO SEEKS TO GROW ABOVE MARKET.

text.p: Finnish information technology group Novo aims to grow faster than the market on average, with a return on investment requirement of at least 15 percent, CEO Jorma Kielenniva said on Monday.

The group said earlier it was applying for a listing on the Brokers' list and may later raise new capital and seek a quotation on the Helsinki main list, to ensure its ability to grow and strengthen its capital structure.
"We have defined a target to grow faster than the market on average," Kielenniva told Reuters in an interview.
Market growth is around 10 percent currently, he added.

Preparing for 2000 millennium compliance and for the advent of the European single currency have boosted overall market growth by some two percentage points, Kielenniva estimated, and said this has made Novo's growth exceptionally strong.
However, he could not specify how much business the two coming events had or would generate.

"But growth must of course be profitable," he added, pointing to a targeted 15 percent return on investment (ROI) for the company, which supplies computer equipment, software and systems and services.

Novo on Monday reported first-quarter profit after financial items at 8.4 million markka, up from 5.3 million in the year-ago period, and its return on investment was 15.4 percent. In 1996, its ROI was 25.9 percent, up from 19.6 percent a year earlier.
Novo is mainly owned by Finnish municipalities, although state-owned bank Postipankki is its second largest owner with an 18 percent stake, he said.

The City of Helsinki holds 22.8 percent, the Association of Finnish Local Authorities owns 13 percent, the City of Vantaa and Espoo 10.9 and 10.8 percent respectively and the municipalities' pension fund owns seven percent.
Postipankki will be Novo's aviser in the flotation.
Kielenniva said the group aims to grow internationally too, mainly in the Baltics and the St Petersburg area, and it also has two niche products which it plans to offer globally.
These are Finnair's FlyTop tax-free shopping logistics system and a mapping system developed together with the Chinese national survey board, he said.
Novo's annual sales growth has been around 20 percent, and last year, net sales rose to 1.14 billion marka from 816 million in 1995 -- a 40 percent increase.
This has come both organically and through acquisitions "and the intention is to continue along those lines," Kielenniva said.
The group wants to maintain an equity-to-assets ratio over 40 percent -- at end-March it stood at 48.3 percent, he added.

Kielenniva declined to say when a listing on the Helsinki main list may happen or how much capital the company aims to raise, but the group has been authorised by shareholders to issue 760,000 shares with a five markka nominal value.

He said its last directed share issue -- before the shares were split by four -- was done at 310 markka per share, corresponding to 77.50 markka now, but added this was not a benchmark for its future market capitalisation.
Novo has 5.59 million shares.
